newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan bourse plans to allow warrant issues.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan bourse plans to allow warrant issues.

text.p: Taiwan Stock Exchange Corp, the island's main stock exchange, said on Wednesday it has completed a proposal to begin allowing local and foreign institutions to issue warrants on Taiwan blue-chip stocks.
"We just completed the proposal, setting initial details for warrants issuance," said an exchange director, Peng Szu-che.
The liberalisation still needs final approval from the market regulating Securities and Exchange Commission."
"The direction to open warrants issuance has been set. Now it's just the matter of when to begin and what are the details," Peng told Reuters by telephone.

The exchange will allow local and foreign banks or securities brokerages to issue warrants on domestic blue chips with a market value of more than T$30 billion and 25 percent or more of their shares circulating in the market, Peng said.
To be eligible, listed companies must also have more than 7,500 shareholders, he said. Peng said more than 20 local listed firms now qualified under the proposed guidelines.
These firms mainly include Cathay Life, Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank, Hua Nan Bank, Nan Ya Plastics, Formosa Plastics and China Steel, he said.
To date, only Morgan Stanley group has expressed an interest to issue warrants here, Peng said.
"Local banks or securities brokerages, which have no previous experience, may have to seek cooperation with foreign counterparts to jointly launch warrants issues," he said.
